name: Inventions & Everyday Things (AI-written, not yet reviewed)
description: 60 questions on inventions and everyday things, from easy to hard (21 easy, 19 medium, 20 hard), written by Claude. Every question and answer needs checking by a person before anybody plays it.

source.name: Written by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) on 2026-10-05, from its own knowledge plus the pages each item cites: no API call. Each item's `source` names the page its fact was confirmed on, or "common knowledge" with a reason where the fact is universal. Fact-check pending: no item carries `checked` yet, so a separate fact-check pass still has to go through every item, and a person still reviews it by playing.

review.how: Check every question, answer and explanation. Fix or delete what is wrong, set status to 'reviewed' with your name and the date, then move the file to packs/ and list it in pack_library.js.

items.question: Who received the 1876 US patent for the telephone?
items.explain: Bell's telephone patent was granted on March 7, 1876.

items.question: Which inventor showed off his electric light bulb at his Menlo Park lab in 1879?
items.explain: Edison's team made a long-lasting bulb in October 1879 and showed it off at Menlo Park.

items.question: The teddy bear is named after which US president?
items.explain: The toy was named for President Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt in 1902.

items.question: Crayola is famous for making what?
items.explain: Crayola crayons have been coloring pictures since 1903.

items.question: Band-Aid is a brand name for what?
items.explain: The Band-Aid is a small bandage with gauze stuck to a sticky strip.

items.question: Blue jeans are usually made from which fabric?
items.explain: Tough cotton denim has been the jeans fabric since the 1870s.

items.question: A Rubik's Cube has how many different colors?
items.explain: Each of the cube's six faces starts out a different color.

items.question: LEGO bricks come from which country?
items.explain: LEGO was started by a Danish carpenter, Ole Kirk Christiansen.

items.question: Mary Anderson invented a device to clear rain and snow from a car's front window. What is it?
items.explain: She patented her wiper blade in 1903 after watching streetcar drivers struggle in the snow.

items.question: A Slinky toy is shaped like what?
items.explain: A Slinky is a long wire wound into a springy coil.

items.question: Teflon is best known as a non-stick coating on what?
items.explain: Teflon is slippery and heat-tolerant, so food slides right off the pan.

items.question: Velcro fastens with tiny hooks on one side and tiny what on the other?
items.explain: Velcro is a hook-and-loop fastener.

items.question: Isaac Singer's name became famous on which household machine?
items.explain: Singer built and sold sewing machines in the 1850s and beyond.

items.question: Charles Goodyear's way of toughening rubber is still used to make which car part?
items.explain: Toughened, 'vulcanized' rubber is what car tires are made from.

items.question: Which toy company makes the Barbie doll?
items.explain: Mattel co-founder Ruth Handler introduced Barbie in 1959.

items.question: Morse code sends letters as patterns of what?
items.explain: Short and long signals, dots and dashes, spell out each letter.

source.note: Morse code being dots and dashes is universally known.

items.question: Post-it notes are what kind of office supply?
items.explain: Post-it notes stick, peel off, and stick again without tearing the page.

items.question: The name Otis is famous on machines that carry people up and down between floors. What are they?
items.explain: Elisha Otis made elevators safe enough for everyday use.

items.question: The 'lead' in an ordinary pencil is actually made mainly of what?
items.explain: Pencil 'lead' is really graphite mixed with clay, with no lead at all.

source.note: That pencil 'lead' is graphite is a widely known everyday fact.

items.question: Window glass is made mainly from melted what?
items.explain: Glass is made by melting sand at very high heat.

source.note: Glass being made from sand is a universally taught everyday fact.

items.question: The pattern of black stripes scanned at a store checkout is called a what?
items.explain: Store barcodes were first scanned at a checkout in 1974.

items.question: Percy Spencer got the idea for the microwave oven when what melted in his pocket?
items.explain: Standing near a radar tube melted his candy bar, and he wondered why.

items.question: A microwave oven heats food mainly by making which molecules vibrate?
items.explain: Vibrating water molecules in the food make the heat that cooks it.

items.question: Art Fry dreamed up the Post-it note while looking for a bookmark that would stay put in what?
items.explain: His paper bookmarks kept falling out of his hymnal at choir practice.

items.question: Which company makes both Post-it notes and Scotch tape?
items.explain: Both sticky inventions came out of 3M's labs.

items.question: George de Mestral got the idea for Velcro from what?
items.explain: The tiny hooks on burrs inspired his hook-and-loop fastener.

items.question: Alexander Graham Bell was born in which country?
items.explain: Bell was born in Edinburgh, Scotland, in 1847.

items.question: Josephine Cochran patented which kitchen appliance in 1886?
items.explain: Tired of chipped dishes, she built the first practical dishwasher herself.

items.question: Edwin Land founded which camera company, famous for instant photos?
items.explain: Land's Polaroid camera, introduced in 1948, developed pictures in moments.

items.question: Nylon was invented by Wallace Carothers at which company?
items.explain: Carothers led basic research at DuPont from 1928.

items.question: Laszlo Biro, who gave his name to the 'biro' ballpoint pen, came from which country?
items.explain: Biro was a Hungarian journalist who wanted ink that dried as fast as newsprint.

items.question: Christopher Sholes's typewriter gave us which keyboard layout still used today?
items.explain: Sholes's typewriter layout is still on most keyboards today.

items.question: Eli Whitney's gin, patented in 1794, pulled the seeds out of which crop?
items.explain: The cotton gin separated sticky seeds from cotton fiber.

items.question: In 1974, the first item ever scanned with a barcode at a store checkout was what?
items.explain: It was a pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum.

items.question: Before it was a toy, Play-Doh was sold as what kind of product?
items.explain: A teacher found the wallpaper cleaner made great modeling clay.

items.question: Which company has made the Etch A Sketch since 1960?
items.explain: Ohio Art bought the license and made it a Christmas hit in 1960.

items.question: The name LEGO comes from Danish words meaning what?
items.explain: 'Leg godt' is Danish for 'play well'.

items.question: Coca-Cola was first sold in 1886 in which city?
items.explain: It was first poured at Jacobs' Pharmacy in Atlanta for five cents a glass.

items.question: In 1873, Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis patented adding what to work pants?
items.explain: Copper rivets at the pocket corners made the first blue jeans tough.

items.question: Earle Dickson invented the Band-Aid in 1921 while working for which company?
items.explain: Dickson was a Johnson & Johnson employee, and the company sold it that same year.

items.question: The word 'zipper' was coined in 1923 by which company, better known for tires and rubber goods?
items.explain: Goodrich named it for the zipping sound it makes.

items.question: Which Swedish-born engineer designed the modern zipper, with small teeth and a slider?
items.explain: Sundback improved Judson's clumsy clasp locker into the zipper we know.

items.question: The name Velcro blends the French word 'velours' (velvet) with which other French word?
items.explain: Velvet loops plus crochet hooks gave us 'Velcro'.

items.question: Roy Plunkett discovered Teflon at DuPont around 1938 while researching what?
items.explain: A refrigerant experiment left behind the slippery white solid now called Teflon.

items.question: Willis Carrier's first scientific air-conditioning system, in 1902, controlled heat and humidity in what?
items.explain: Controlling humidity helped the printing plant's paper and ink behave.

items.question: At New York's Crystal Palace in 1854, Elisha Otis proved his safety elevator by having what cut?
items.explain: The cable was cut with an axe while he rode the platform, and it held fast.

items.question: Charles Goodyear 'vulcanized' rubber by heating it mixed with which substance?
items.explain: Rubber and sulfur dropped on a hot stove showed him the way.

items.question: Before his traffic signal, Garrett Morgan patented a 1912 'safety hood'. It was an early form of what?
items.explain: His safety hood let wearers breathe in smoky air.

items.question: Richard Drew invented masking tape at 3M in 1925 to help which workers?
items.explain: Painters needed a tape that would mask off two-tone car paint jobs cleanly.

items.question: Walter Hunt dreamed up the safety pin while twisting wire and worrying about a debt of how much?
items.explain: He sold the patent rights, paid the debt, and had money left over.

items.question: Margaret Knight built an 1868 machine that made paper bags with what new feature?
items.explain: Her machine replaced V-shaped bags with the flat-bottomed grocery bag.

items.question: What was the first message Samuel Morse sent over his Baltimore-to-Washington telegraph line in 1844?
items.explain: The famous message went from Baltimore to Washington on May 24, 1844.

items.question: What was the first microwave oven, sold from 1947, called?
items.explain: The first Radarange stood about 6 feet tall and weighed some 750 pounds.

items.question: Before going national as Post-it notes in 1980, the product was test-marketed in 1977 under what name?
items.explain: Press n' Peel tried four cities first, then got a better name.

items.question: The first store barcode scan, on June 26, 1974, took place at a Marsh supermarket in which Ohio city?
items.explain: A pack of gum scanned in Troy, Ohio, started the barcode era.

items.question: Cleveland candy maker Clarence Crane created Life Savers to keep sales up during which season, when chocolate sold slowly?
items.explain: Chocolate melted and sold poorly in hot weather, so mints filled the gap.

items.question: The gray picture on an Etch A Sketch is drawn in a mixture of tiny plastic beads and what?
items.explain: Static holds the aluminum powder to the screen until a stylus scrapes it away.

items.question: The Frisbee got its name from a Connecticut company that made what?
items.explain: College students tossed empty pie tins from the Frisbie Baking Company.

items.question: What did Erno Rubik originally call his puzzle cube in 1974?
items.explain: The Magic Cube was renamed for its inventor when it went worldwide in 1980.

items.question: Who suggested the name Coca-Cola and wrote it out in its famous flowing script?
items.explain: Pemberton's bookkeeper thought 'the two Cs would look well in advertising'.
